name: Lead
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists lead among metals corroded by acetic acid. The 2025 study describes copper and lead as very sensitive to formic acid and states that carboxylic acids are known to corrode copper and lead.

name: Copper and copper alloys
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists copper and bronze as corroded by benzoic acid and formic acid, and by hydrogen sulfide and carbonyl sulfide. The 2025 study states that carboxylic acids are known to corrode copper and lead.

name: Silver
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists silver as corroded by hydrogen sulfide and carbonyl sulfide. Silver is also one of the three metals used in the Oddy test.

name: Paper
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists paper weakening from formic acid emitted by oil-based coatings.

name: Black-and-white photographic material
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists darkening of silver particles in black and white photographs from hydrogen peroxide emitted by fresh alkyd or oil-based coatings.

name: 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidinol (TMP-ol)
notes: Reported as a component of hindered amine light stabilizers such as Tinuvin 770, which the NMAI study identifies as an additive of the Terostat structural adhesive.

name: Plasticizer from degraded flexible PVC
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 does not name a specific plasticizer, and neither does ArtifactGuard.

name: Benzoic acid
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists benzoic acid from degraded plasticizer from flexible PVC as corroding copper and bronze.

name: Acetic acid
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists acetic acid as corroding lead. In the 2025 study the two materials with the largest normalized acetic acid peak areas produced the most severe lead corrosion. Lead acetates identified on lead coupons in the cellulose ether study indicate acetic acid in the test tube.

name: Formic acid
notes: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists formic acid as corroding copper and bronze and weakening paper. The 2025 study describes copper and lead as very sensitive to it.

name: Carboxylic acids (class-level detection)
notes: Reported at class level by HS-SPME and DTD. Individual acids are named only where the paper names them.

name: Lactic acid
notes: Detected by HS-SPME and DTD in the polylactic acid filament.

name: Lactide
notes: Detected by HS-SPME and DTD in the polylactic acid filament.

name: Sulphur-containing compounds (unspecified)
notes: Reported as a compound class; the paper does not name individual sulphur compounds.

name: TCPP (phosphate flame retardant)
notes: The 2025 study notes that flame retardants have been associated with corrosive reactions involving metals.

name: Glycol derivatives
notes: The 2025 study notes that glycols can contribute to the softening of other plastic materials in their proximity.

name: Phthalates
notes: Esters of phthalic acid used as plasticizers.

name: Formaldehyde
notes: Detected in small amount from a hydroxypropyl cellulose sample.

name: Representative 3-in-1 Oddy protocol
notes: The interlaboratory review reports the 3-in-1 version, 60 °C and 2 g of material as common practice, and 28 days at 60 °C in Oddy's original description. Other variables are not standardized.

name: Terostat-9220
manufacturer: Not named in the cited papers

label: Casework use, 2009–2014
identityNote: The 2025 review names Terostat-9220 as the source of TMP-ol. The NMAI study reports that the case manufacturer used two formulations, Terostat MS 937 and Terostat 9220, and that only Terostat 937 has been found in the NMAI cases. The cited passages do not say which formulation was Oddy tested.

institution: Museum staff (institution not named in the cited papers)

method: SPME–GC–MS and DART-MS on exhibit-case materials (NMAI study)
observedEffect: TMP-ol was identified as the organic component of white crystalline efflorescence on exhibited objects and as emitted by the structural adhesive used in display-case construction (Terostat MS 937 in the NMAI study; the 2025 review names Terostat-9220).

method: preventive-conservation guidance (CCI Technical Bulletin 32, direct-contact damage)
observedEffect: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists plasticizer from degraded flexible PVC as causing stains (discolouration or yellowing) and embrittlement, and viscous plasticizer exudate as leaching compounds from an object's surface.

method: preventive-conservation guidance (CCI Technical Bulletin 32, airborne pollutants)
observedEffect: CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists benzoic acid from degraded plasticizer from flexible PVC as an airborne pollutant that corrodes copper and bronze.

effect: In enclosed display cases, TMP-ol emitted by the adhesive reacted with acidic compounds from other case materials to form white crystalline deposits on exhibited objects. The NMAI study summarizes Rijksmuseum findings of such acids emitted by peroxide-cured silicone gaskets, MDF panels, UV adhesive and beeswax products. Whether acid sources are present in your case is not part of this scenario.

CCI Technical Bulletin 32 lists plasticizer from degraded flexible PVC as causing stains and embrittlement in direct contact, and viscous plasticizer exudate as leaching compounds from an object's surface. The condition of the PVC is not part of this scenario.

The 2025 study notes, citing earlier work, that phthalates can migrate from the source and be incorporated into adjacent objects, causing plasticization or softening that can affect object integrity and have a negative visual impact.

statement: The Terostat adhesive passed an Oddy test conducted by museum staff.
scope: as vetted by museum staff; formulation, protocol and date are not stated in the cited papers

statement: An Oddy PASS alone establishes that the Terostat adhesive is compatible with objects in a display case.
rationale: A 2025 review reports that the adhesive passed the Oddy test conducted by museum staff because it does not react corrosively with the metal substrates, yet caused significant issues in display cases: white crystalline efflorescence on objects at several institutions. The screening test did not identify the emitted compound or its reaction with acids from other materials in the case.
